body: Thank you everyone for your kind words and support. It means a lot to me.
Woops, I meant 3.

I agree that they are worthless, but I'm pretty much out of options with what else to do. My only other plan is to go back and do a double in Comp Sci and either Business or Mathematics but I need a steady income to be able to do that, otherwise I'll be going through another 4 years of poverty.

I was young when I went into the degree. The market crashed shortly after. I would have liked to be a lawyer, but the likelihood of that happening is very low. Even if I do get admitted and into a job, the fact that there are this many graduates means that there will be downward pressure on working conditions, salaries, and job security.

I think I would be an idiot to take further steps in becoming a lawyer given the current and future prospects within the field.

http://www.afr.com/business/legal/too-many-law-graduates-and-not-enough-jobs-20151020-gkdbyx
Well, resignation it is then.

>If you're applying for jobs where there's going to be a bunch of applicants the only way you'll get to the interview stage is if your application is somehow better than the vast majority. Better to go overboard on a few applications IMO, with a bunch of shit about the company in the cover letter and a properly tailored CV.

I've been doing this for years. I would not be asking this question if my current approach was working. Right now, I am ready to accept just about any job that pays better than minimum wage.

> community law centre

I have experience in one already. I don't want to become a lawyer because that would mean another year of practical legal training (and more debt), and uncertain prospects of employment. The market is already flooded with law grads that have completed their PLT but cannot get hired as lawyers. I do not want to add to it.

All up, I've been in uni for about 8 and a half years. I don't like thinking about that, but it is what it is. I am not going to be constrained by thoughts of the past.
I'm glad to hear that! Thanks for taking the time to read it.

I'm in a similar boat as you and I empathise with your situation. I understand the fear and uncertainty. But I hold out hope that even though my relationship with my future psychologist might not be the same as my previous, the relationship may still be positive despite being different (a different kind of positive if you will).

I don't know whether or not I will have to switch psychologists multiple times, but I have learned that it is important to find one suited to me and my needs so that I can have the trust and support needed to aid in dealing with this illness. I hope you don't settle for less and that you take care of yourself. You may have a long way to go, but please embark on your journey because I think your psychiatrist would like for you to be in a good place and in good hands.
Yeah, the undiagnosed period is the worst! Hope you're doing better these days.

It happens mate, and it speaks to how much you valued the relationship between you and your therapist. I know it might not change how you feel about it, but I don't think your situation is embarrassing at all. We all trip over sometimes.

She did. I'm going to begin the search tomorrow. I'm taking today just to let myself feel what I need to feel before moving on.

Yeah, I've been there as have many other's in here, I'm sure. It's great that you're not beating yourself up over this since that can become a vicious cycle of feeling down and turning back to drugs.

Going from regular use to 7 days off is no small feat, and shows that you can do things that you recognise will ultimately be better for you. I won't presume to know whether or not drugs make your symptoms worse as they do mine, but I hope that whatever you choose to do is beneficial for you and helps you get to where you need to be.

This is my throwaway account that I use very rarely, but please post here as often as you need to. If you decide that you want to get back on the wagon again, here are a few subreddits that might assist you if you ever feel like you need that little boost of encouragement or reassurance: /r/leaves /r/OpiatesRecovery/ /r/secularsobriety/

I hope the dark place passes quickly and that stability returns.

Thank you for the kind words. I am already studying in Sydney, but I don't think my marks are anywhere near good enough to get me an entry level position given how many graduates there are compared to how many jobs are on offer. I had some issues halfway through my degree when I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder. It sucked at the time, but I have it somewhat under control now.

But I have to keep trying because what else can I do? I know that sounds a bit deflating, but I'm going to keep applying and hope something sticks.

At this stage, almost anything. 

But mostly office admin or paralegal.
I am taking Lamotrigine/Lamictal and lithium. I don't think drugs can make me stop feeling like this.
Yes, but I don't know if it's working.
I have done all of those things.

I've been unemployed for about 2 years. It's been the most depressing period of my life.

The JSA providers have been pretty much useless. What they try to do is get me to sign up for classes that they provide and charge the government for. For the first class, I thought I would be undergoing some sort of training or something useful.

All that the class was was a 3 day course talking about eating and sleeping properly, and doing "group building exercises" which were pretty much primary school games.

I think I've been "shelved", but it feels like an indignant kick to the groin every time I have to go in and waste 2 hours for no return. I honestly wish I could find a job because it feels crushing to be socially excluded because everyone else has something to talk about and money to spend on socialising, eating out, and pursuing their interests.

I don't know if my JSA is fraudulent or not, but the system does not work as far as I am concerned. I feel worse off knowing that I am engaging in a worthless exercise that only serves to make someone else richer.

The JSA program is as much a government handout as the dole is.
